considered.reasoning: This changes the economic content of the financing leg rather than stacking two already-measured price legs: capping repurchases at contemporaneous operating cash flow and zeroing them for cash-negative firms separates genuine price judgments from levered financial engineering, which is the one contamination of the mix ratio that the generation-5 tests never addressed. The construction stays inside the bounded composition form that has driven every large alpha in the archive, so a decline would be evidence that debt-funded repurchases carry the same information — an economically interesting result either way.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Scale consistent neutral placement of non payers
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ebitda, ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), ADD(dltt, dlc)))), RANK(COALESCE(RATIO(SUB(prstkc, dvt), ADD(prstkc, dvt)), SIGN(SUB(prstkc, dvt)))))
considered.hypothesis: Firms that distribute nothing have made no instrument choice and belong exactly at the midpoint of the buyback-versus-dividend scale, so the earlier alpha loss from widening the sample may reflect a mis-scaled fallback rather than genuine dilution of the mechanism by non-payers.
considered.reasoning: The previous widening used (prstkc − dvt)/at as the fallback, which lives on a completely different scale from the bounded [−1, 1] mix and therefore scattered non-payers unpredictably through the ranking rather than placing them neutrally; SIGN evaluates to exactly zero when both flows are absent and to ±1 in the same units as the mix itself, so the fallback is scale-correct by construction. This makes the coverage question decidable for the first time — if alpha now holds at coverage near 0.12, the mechanism is universal and the earlier decay was a units artifact; if it still decays, non-payers genuinely carry no instrument-choice information.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Buyback tilt in excess of the flexibility motive
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ebitda, ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), ADD(dltt, dlc)))), SUB(RANK(RATIO(SUB(prstkc, dvt), ADD(prstkc, dvt))), RANK(VOL(RATIO(ib, at), 5))))
considered.hypothesis: Earnings instability mechanically pushes firms toward repurchases because dividends are sticky commitments, so the price-revealing part of the buyback tilt is the portion in excess of what a firm's earnings volatility already implies.
considered.reasoning: Subtracting the volatility rank from the mix rank removes the flexibility-driven component of the instrument choice instead of multiplying by it, so the long leg is populated by firms whose buyback tilt is unusually high *given* their earnings instability rather than by low-volatility quality firms — precisely the confound the critic identified in the multiplicative version. The residual construction is scale-consistent (both terms are percentiles), and because the volatility term enters with a negative sign the signal cannot inherit the documented low-risk anomaly's long-side exposure.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Normalized firm level yield with wide mix
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(MA(ebitda, 3), ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), ADD(dltt, dlc)))), RANK(COALESCE(RATIO(SUB(prstkc, dvt), ADD(prstkc, dvt)), SIGN(SUB(prstkc, dvt)))))
considered.hypothesis: The price benchmark that governs a repurchase is the whole firm's price relative to its normal earning power, so combining enterprise-level pricing with three-year averaged operating earnings should classify cyclical troughs — where undervalued repurchasers concentrate — better than either correction alone.
considered.reasoning: The two price-leg corrections that have worked address orthogonal errors — one fixes the claim being priced (equity versus whole firm), the other fixes transitory noise in the earnings numerator — and a cyclically adjusted enterprise yield is a distinct valuation concept rather than a blend of two ranked legs. Pairing it with the wide mix tests the best available measurement of both sides on the full cross-section, which is the natural candidate for the final consolidated signal.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Where the incremental payout dollar went
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ebitda, ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), ADD(dltt, dlc)))), RANK(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(prstkc, 1), DELTA(dvt, 1)), ADD(ABS(DELTA(prstkc, 1)), ABS(DELTA(dvt, 1))))))
considered.hypothesis: A standing payout mix is inherited policy, while the allocation of this year's *incremental* payout dollars is a fresh decision made at today's price, so the marginal split between added repurchases and added dividends should carry the news content of the mechanism.
considered.reasoning: This differs from the previously tested change-in-ratio (alpha 2.5%) because it forms the composition directly from the two flow changes rather than differencing a bounded ratio, which avoids the artifact that a firm pinned at +1 for years shows zero change despite large new buybacks. Normalizing by the sum of absolute changes keeps it bounded and interpretable, and a strong result would mean the signal refreshes annually rather than being a slow-moving firm characteristic — directly relevant to how it should be traded.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Buyback tilt beyond dividend paying tradition
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ebitda, ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), ADD(dltt, dlc)))), SUB(RANK(RATIO(SUB(prstkc, dvt), ADD(prstkc, dvt))), RANK(TS_SUM(INDICATOR(dvt, 0), 5))))
considered.hypothesis: Most of the cross-sectional variation in payout composition is firm type — companies that have never paid a dividend sit permanently at the buyback extreme — so the price-revealing part is the buyback tilt in excess of what a firm's five-year record of dividend paying already implies.
considered.reasoning: The single most serious remaining challenge to the champion is that the mix leg is a disguised never-paid-a-dividend indicator interacted with value; subtracting the dividend-tradition rank removes that static component and leaves genuine deviation, following the orthogonalization design that preserved full alpha when applied to earnings volatility. If alpha survives here as well, the mechanism is established as an active managerial decision rather than a firm-type classification, which is the key robustness question for the final consolidation.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Magnitude preserving discount with wide mix
considered.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(ebitda, ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), ADD(dltt, dlc))), 1)), RANK(COALESCE(RATIO(SUB(prstkc, dvt), ADD(prstkc, dvt)), SIGN(SUB(prstkc, dvt)))))
considered.hypothesis: The value transferred to continuing shareholders by a buyback-tilted payout is proportional to the *size* of the discount, not to its rank, so the price leg should enter in magnitude units: a firm at twice the industry-relative enterprise yield should count roughly twice as much, which percentile ranking flattens away.
considered.reasoning: Every configuration tested so far has ranked the price leg, which imposes a uniform distribution and discards exactly the dispersion the accretion mechanism says is priced; replacing the rank with a winsorized industry z-score is a functional-form change dictated by the economics rather than another blend of two already-measured legs, so its outcome is not bounded by its parents. It also changes portfolio construction materially — the long leg will concentrate on genuinely deep discounts rather than on the top decile by ordering — which is the untested question of whether the spread is driven by discount depth or merely by ordinal position.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Buyback tilt beyond what leverage permits
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ebitda, ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), ADD(dltt, dlc)))), SUB(RANK(RATIO(SUB(prstkc, dvt), ADD(prstkc, dvt))), RANK(RATIO(lt, at))))
considered.hypothesis: Leverage mechanically shapes payout composition — heavily obligated firms cannot commit to a sticky dividend and default to discretionary repurchases or to nothing — so the price-revealing part of the buyback tilt is the portion in excess of what a firm's obligation load already dictates.
considered.reasoning: This addresses a confound distinct from the two already handled: earnings volatility captures cash-flow risk and dividend tradition captures firm type, whereas the liability ratio captures balance-sheet capacity to make fixed commitments, and it is the confound most likely to be correlated with the enterprise price leg since both involve debt. Unlike swapping dvc for dvt — which would move only the small subset of preferred-paying firms — this reweights the entire cross-section, and because the leverage rank enters negatively the long leg cannot inherit a low-leverage quality tilt.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Pure discretion in the payout choice
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ebitda, ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), ADD(dltt, dlc)))), SUB(RANK(RATIO(SUB(prstkc, dvt), ADD(prstkc, dvt))), SUMRANK(VOL(RATIO(ib, at), 5), TS_SUM(INDICATOR(dvt, 0), 5))))
considered.hypothesis: Two forces mechanically determine payout composition without any reference to price — unstable earnings make dividends unattractive, and firms that have never paid one keep not paying — so subtracting both jointly leaves the residual tilt that can only reflect a judgment about the share price.
considered.reasoning: This is a residualization against a composite of the two known non-price drivers rather than an average of a level and its own first difference, so the outcome is not an interpolation between tested parents: it either shows that the discretionary residual carries the full alpha, confirming the managerial-judgment interpretation, or that stripping both motives destroys it, which would reclassify the champion as a firm-type-times-value effect. The single-purge version retained alpha at 5.2% with t=4.34, so double purging is the decisive robustness test to run before the final consolidation, and both subtracted terms are percentiles on the same scale as the mix rank.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Wide sample discretion residual
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ebitda, ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), ADD(dltt, dlc)))), SUB(RANK(COALESCE(RATIO(SUB(prstkc, dvt), ADD(prstkc, dvt)), SIGN(SUB(prstkc, dvt)))), SUMRANK(VOL(RATIO(ib, at), 5), TS_SUM(INDICATOR(dvt, 0), 5))))
considered.hypothesis: The discretion residual should be defined for every firm, not only distributors: a non-payer has made no instrument choice and belongs at the neutral midpoint before the mechanical motives are removed, so the purged signal should extend to the full cross-section without losing its economic content.
considered.reasoning: The purge terms — earnings volatility and dividend-paying history — are already computable for the whole panel, so the 0.074 coverage of the best signal is imposed entirely by the payer-only mix, an asymmetry the scale-correct SIGN fallback removes at no economic cost. This is the one change that can lift the archive's best alpha design to the 0.12 coverage that the wide-mix family has repeatedly shown is attainable while retaining alpha above 5%.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Rebalanced discretion residual
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ebitda, ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), ADD(dltt, dlc)))), RANK(SUB(RANK(RATIO(SUB(prstkc, dvt), ADD(prstkc, dvt))), SUMRANK(VOL(RATIO(ib, at), 5), TS_SUM(INDICATOR(dvt, 0), 5)))))
considered.hypothesis: The economic content of the discretion residual is its ordering of firms by price-motivated buyback tilt, not the arbitrary spacing of the difference between two percentiles, so re-ranking the residual before interacting it with the discount should preserve the mechanism while producing a balanced portfolio.
considered.reasoning: Every residualized signal in generation 7 kept a high FF5 alpha but suffered a badly degraded Sharpe (0.05–0.40), the signature of an unevenly spaced sorting variable that concentrates mass in the middle and produces thin, factor-exposed extreme deciles; re-ranking restores uniform spacing so the decile portfolios carry equal firm counts. This isolates a single structural choice — raw residual versus re-ranked residual — against the archive's best signal, and it is the most likely route to a design that is simultaneously strong on alpha, alpha t-stat and Sharpe.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: New dollars directed to buybacks
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ebitda, ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), ADD(dltt, dlc)))), RANK(RATIO(SUB(MUL(DELTA(prstkc, 1), INDICATOR(DELTA(prstkc, 1), 0)), MUL(DELTA(dvt, 1), INDICATOR(DELTA(dvt, 1), 0))), ADD(MUL(DELTA(prstkc, 1), INDICATOR(DELTA(prstkc, 1), 0)), MUL(DELTA(dvt, 1), INDICATOR(DELTA(dvt, 1), 0))))))
considered.hypothesis: The fresh decision each year is where a firm sends its *additional* payout dollars, and only genuine increases count: a dividend cut is a distress event, not a redirection of new capital toward repurchases, and should not be scored as a bullish instrument choice.
considered.reasoning: This repairs the identified flaw in the marginal-flow construction, where a large negative dividend change mechanically pushed a firm into the long leg even with no new buyback; taking positive parts of both flow changes means the ratio compares incremental buyback dollars against incremental dividend dollars and is undefined for firms that increased neither. That correction targets exactly the contaminated cell that plausibly held the earlier version's alpha down to 1.8% despite its strong FMB slope of 6.23.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Equity priced discretion residual
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(ib, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)))), SUB(RANK(RATIO(SUB(prstkc, dvt), ADD(prstkc, dvt))), SUMRANK(VOL(RATIO(ib, at), 5), TS_SUM(INDICATOR(dvt, 0), 5))))
considered.hypothesis: A repurchase transacts in the equity claim, so once the financing leg is purged of non-price motives the relevant discount may be the equity multiple rather than the enterprise multiple, which prices claims the buyback does not touch.
considered.reasoning: The two price legs have only ever been compared against the raw mix, where the enterprise version won on FMB and the equity blend won on alpha t-stat and Sharpe; with the purged financing leg now established as the strongest construct, this crossing decides which discount definition to carry into the final generation. The two legs rank materially different firms — financials and asset-light companies are priced only by the equity blend — so the outcome is not mechanically bounded by the enterprise-multiple parent.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Discretion residual with graded dividend commitment
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ebitda, ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), ADD(dltt, dlc)))), SUB(RANK(RATIO(SUB(prstkc, dvt), ADD(prstkc, dvt))), SUMRANK(VOL(RATIO(ib, at), 5), MA(RATIO(dvt, at), 3))))
considered.hypothesis: The strength of a firm's standing dividend commitment, not merely the binary fact that it paid in some years, is what mechanically pins its payout composition, so purging the mix of a graded three-year dividend intensity isolates price-motivated instrument choice more cleanly than purging it of a coarse payer count.
considered.reasoning: This drops the size term entirely — the critic is right that subtracting a market-cap rank mechanically promotes microcaps into the long leg and confounds the judgment interpretation with a size tilt — and instead repairs the weaker of the two existing purge terms, whose 0-to-5 integer scale creates large rank ties and which alone produced an FMB slope of −0.50. A continuous commitment measure should yield a smoother residual with better cross-sectional resolution, addressing precisely the spacing problem that has depressed the Sharpe of every residualized version while leaving the 6.7% alpha mechanism intact.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Buybacks measured in dividends at a discount
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ebitda, ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), ADD(dltt, dlc)))), RANK(LOG(RATIO(ADD(prstkc, dvt), dvt))))
considered.hypothesis: Among firms that have already proved their cash generation by committing to a dividend, the informative quantity is how many dividends' worth of its own stock management chose to buy on top of that commitment — a continuous measure of conviction that the bounded mix ratio compresses into a ceiling.
considered.reasoning: The mix ratio pins every zero-dividend repurchaser at exactly +1, so a large tie block occupies the long decile and the signal cannot distinguish a token buyback from one worth ten years of dividends; expressing repurchases in units of the firm's own dividend and taking logs restores resolution exactly where the spread is formed. This also asks a question the archive cannot currently answer — whether the alpha comes from the payer-type contrast or from graded conviction among committed payers — which directly determines the construction of the final consolidated signal, rather than merely re-testing an existing series with a lag applied.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Wide rebalanced discretion residual
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ebitda, ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), ADD(dltt, dlc)))), RANK(SUB(RANK(COALESCE(RATIO(SUB(prstkc, dvt), ADD(prstkc, dvt)), SIGN(SUB(prstkc, dvt)))), SUMRANK(VOL(RATIO(ib, at), 5), TS_SUM(INDICATOR(dvt, 0), 5)))))
considered.hypothesis: The price-motivated component of the payout instrument choice — the mix stripped of the earnings-instability and dividend-tradition motives — predicts returns when interacted with a firm-level discount, and it should be measured on the whole cross-section with an evenly spaced sorting variable.
considered.reasoning: The two fixes have each been validated in isolation against the same base but never combined: widening the sample with the scale-correct SIGN fallback raised alpha from 6.7% to 7.7% and coverage from 0.074 to 0.110, while re-ranking the residual raised the FMB slope from 5.11 to 6.13 and Sharpe from 0.396 to 0.525. Because they act on different defects — sample truncation versus the sign inversion created by multiplying a negative residual by a positive price rank — their gains should be close to additive, making this the leading candidate for a signal that is simultaneously strong on slope, alpha magnitude, alpha reliability and Sharpe.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Wide rebalanced residual with graded commitment
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ebitda, ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), ADD(dltt, dlc)))), RANK(SUB(RANK(COALESCE(RATIO(SUB(prstkc, dvt), ADD(prstkc, dvt)), SIGN(SUB(prstkc, dvt)))), SUMRANK(VOL(RATIO(ib, at), 5), MA(RATIO(dvt, at), 3)))))
considered.hypothesis: What pins a firm's payout composition is the strength of its standing dividend commitment, measured continuously, rather than the coarse count of years in which it happened to pay something.
considered.reasoning: The graded three-year dividend-intensity purge lifted the cross-sectional slope from 5.11 to 5.92 relative to the payer-count purge while holding alpha at 6.2%, indicating that the count's integer ties were degrading resolution; applying it inside the wide, re-ranked construction tests whether that resolution gain survives once the two structural fixes are in place. Running it alongside Signal 1 isolates the purge measurement as the single varied element, so the final choice between the two is directly interpretable.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Dual priced wide rebalanced residual
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(ebitda, ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), ADD(dltt, dlc))), SUMRANK(RATIO(ib, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))))), RANK(SUB(RANK(COALESCE(RATIO(SUB(prstkc, dvt), ADD(prstkc, dvt)), SIGN(SUB(prstkc, dvt)))), SUMRANK(VOL(RATIO(ib, at), 5), TS_SUM(INDICATOR(dvt, 0), 5)))))
considered.hypothesis: A repurchase transacts the equity claim while its funding capacity is a firm-level property, so the discount that governs the decision is best measured by combining enterprise and equity multiples, which price different firms and fail in different places.
considered.reasoning: The evidence now justifies a blend rather than a horse race: against the identical purged financing leg, the equity composite delivered higher alpha (7.1% versus 6.7%) while the enterprise multiple delivered a much higher slope (5.11 versus 3.84), so each is capturing pricing information the other misses. Weighting the enterprise leg at one half and the two equity yields at a quarter each matches that measured pattern, and the union covers financial and asset-light firms that the enterprise multiple alone ranks poorly.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Normalized firm yield with rebalanced residual
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(MA(ebitda, 3), ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), ADD(dltt, dlc)))), RANK(SUB(RANK(COALESCE(RATIO(SUB(prstkc, dvt), ADD(prstkc, dvt)), SIGN(SUB(prstkc, dvt)))), SUMRANK(VOL(RATIO(ib, at), 5), TS_SUM(INDICATOR(dvt, 0), 5)))))
considered.hypothesis: Management compares its share price against normal earning power rather than a single year's operating result, so a three-year averaged enterprise yield is the discount measure that best identifies genuinely undervalued repurchasers, especially at cyclical troughs.
considered.reasoning: The cyclically adjusted enterprise yield produced the archive's best Sharpe (0.580) and a strong slope (6.67) when paired with the raw wide mix, so pairing it with the purged, re-ranked financing leg tests whether the time-series normalization of the price leg and the motive-purging of the financing leg are complementary. It also directly addresses the risk that earnings-volatility purging tilts the sample toward stable firms while a single-year EBITDA misprices the cyclical ones that remain.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Two year stance discretion residual
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ebitda, ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), ADD(dltt, dlc)))), RANK(SUB(RANK(COALESCE(RATIO(TS_SUM(SUB(prstkc, dvt), 2), TS_SUM(ADD(prstkc, dvt), 2)), SIGN(SUB(prstkc, dvt)))), SUMRANK(VOL(RATIO(ib, at), 5), TS_SUM(INDICATOR(dvt, 0), 5)))))
considered.hypothesis: Management's price-contingent instrument choice is best read over the last two years of cumulative distributions, which captures both the standing stance and the allocation of recently generated cash while averaging out the lumpiness of a single tender offer.
considered.reasoning: This replaces the five-term fusion of two separate financing legs with a single, interpretable measurement change — the window over which the payout composition is cumulated — so the result is attributable against the accepted one-year version by exactly one knob. It also makes no coverage promise it cannot keep: the two-year cumulation is subsumed by the five-year purge terms that already bind, and cumulating over two years rather than one strictly reduces the 0/0 cases that the SIGN fallback must handle, while the three-year version of this same cumulation previously delivered the best Sharpe of its generation.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Current state discretion residual
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ebitda, ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), ADD(dltt, dlc)))), RANK(SUB(RANK(COALESCE(RATIO(SUB(prstkc, dvt), ADD(prstkc, dvt)), SIGN(SUB(prstkc, dvt)))), SUMRANK(VOL(RATIO(ib, at), 3), RATIO(dvt, at)))))
considered.hypothesis: The two motives that mechanically shape payout composition are both current-state properties — how unstable recent earnings are and how large a dividend the firm is currently carrying — so neither requires a five-year history to measure, and purging on contemporaneous quantities should isolate the same discretionary residual on a much larger sample.
considered.reasoning: The previous version was internally inconsistent because the binding history requirement was the five-year dividend-payer count, not the volatility window; replacing that count with the current dividend-to-assets ratio removes the long-history constraint from both purge terms at once, so the coverage argument now actually follows from the expression. It is also an economic improvement rather than a lookback tweak: a continuous measure of the dividend a firm is presently carrying describes its commitment far better than counting how many of the last five years it paid anything, and the graded-commitment purge already raised the cross-sectional slope from 5.11 to 5.92 when tested at a three-year horizon.
considered.author: proposer

critic_notes.target_name: Value plus net payout yield
critic_notes.rationale: This is a plain additive rank blend of two thoroughly published anomalies (book-to-market and net payout yield à la Boudoukh et al. / Daniel-Titman net issuance) with no genuine interaction, so it is a rediscovery whose only contribution is portfolio averaging.

critic_notes.target_name: Earnings yield times float shrinkage
critic_notes.rationale: Both legs (E/P and net share issuance via share-count growth) are well-known standalone anomalies, but the multiplicative rank form is a genuine (if mild) superadditive interaction that concentrates exposure in the joint tails and is internally consistent with the positive expected sign; the incremental information over a simple average is the open question.

critic_notes.target_name: Enterprise cheapness less total external financing
critic_notes.rationale: The financing leg is essentially Bradshaw-Richardson-Sloan net external financing and the valuation leg is EBITDA/EV, so the difference is a re-labeled combination of two published anomalies, and the enterprise-value denominator can go negative for net-cash firms, which flips the ratio's sign and systematically misranks exactly the cash-rich firms the hypothesis cares about.

critic_notes.target_name: Issuance purged book-to-market
critic_notes.rationale: Embedding cumulative net issuance inside the book-equity numerator rather than adding a second sorting leg is a substantively different construction from the standard two-signal blend, the expression matches the hypothesis and expected sign, and its main risks (sstk/prstkc coverage and overlap with Daniel-Titman's B/M decomposition) are testable rather than disqualifying.

critic_notes.target_name: Cash flow yield times deleveraging
critic_notes.rationale: Routing the financing channel through debt flows is a defensible way to differentiate from buyback-based signals, but a large mass of firms have dltis=dltr=0, making the second rank near-degenerate over a wide swath of the cross-section, and net debt retirement is mechanically correlated with high operating cash flow, so the "interaction" may add little beyond the cash-flow-yield leg.

critic_notes.target_name: Financing conditioned valuation split
critic_notes.rationale: The stated hypothesis claims valuation carries opposite information across financing regimes, but the expression preserves the same direction in both subsamples (cheap issuers still score above expensive issuers, just shifted into [-1,0]), so it does not test the claimed reversal; it merely reproduces the "long cheap repurchasers, short expensive issuers" composite of the earlier proposals with two non-comparable, discontinuously spliced rank scales.

critic_notes.target_name: Cheapness with liability contraction
critic_notes.rationale: This is structurally the archived "Cash flow yield times deleveraging" with the value leg swapped from oancf/P to ib/P and the financing leg swapped from (dltr−dltis)/at to −Δlt/lt — a variable substitution motivated by coverage rather than a new mechanism, and both legs (earnings yield, liability/asset growth) are themselves well-published anomalies whose simple rank product adds little.

critic_notes.target_name: Sales yield confirmed by dividend commitment
critic_notes.rationale: The S/P leg is deliberately chosen to be least collinear with HML and the dividend-change conditioner is a genuinely different confirmation channel from the buyback-based archive, but the second leg will be exactly zero for the large non-payer majority, so a big tied mass gets a mid rank and the interaction collapses toward plain sales-to-price over much of the cross-section — the tie handling should be checked before reading any result.

critic_notes.target_name: Industry neutral cheap repurchaser
critic_notes.rationale: Industry neutralization of a cheap-repurchaser composite is a legitimate and non-trivial design change with a clean single-variable contrast against the archive, though the stated diagnosis is loose — FF5's HML/CMA are not sector portfolios, so sector spanning is an unlikely explanation for the archive's null alphas, and the test is better framed as a straightforward neutralization experiment than as a confirmation of that story.

critic_notes.target_name: Payout in excess of valuation implied norm
critic_notes.rationale: The hypothesis claims a "residual" from an implied financing norm, but a difference of two ranks is not a projection — it imposes a unit *negative* loading on book-to-market, so the construction deliberately goes short the value premium while the expected sign is positive, meaning a positive result requires the financing leg to overwhelm a mechanically adverse value tilt and a null result will be uninterpretable.

critic_notes.target_name: Financing policy reversal at cheap prices
critic_notes.rationale: Moving from the persistent level of net equity issuance to its year-over-year change is a substantive information-content change rather than a rescaling, it is internally consistent in sign, and it gives a clean test of whether the archive family's null alphas reflect staleness — the main risks are the noisiness of a differenced cash-flow flow item and the post-SCF coverage ceiling.

critic_notes.target_name: Value slope gated by net cash returned
critic_notes.rationale: This repeats the exact ZSCORE(value)×RANK(financing) architecture of the archived "Levered buyback conviction" that already failed, and because Δlt dwarfs dvt for most firms the gate is effectively −liability growth, making it economically the same bet as this batch's "Cheapness with liability contraction" proposal rather than an independent test.

critic_notes.target_name: Industry neutral cash release
critic_notes.rationale: This is the archive's "Discounted cash released by payout" with RANK mechanically swapped for IND_RANK on both legs — a normalization variant applying a transform already shown to work elsewhere in the archive, not a new economic mechanism, and it inherits the che-denominator instability (dvt/che explodes for low-cash payers) that likely drives the FMB-vs-alpha gap more than sector loadings do.

critic_notes.target_name: Industry neutral financing reversal
critic_notes.rationale: A purely cosmetic crossing of two archived signals — leg one is verbatim the IND_RANK(ib/mcap) from "Industry neutral cheap repurchaser" and leg two is verbatim the DELTA net-repurchase term from "Financing policy reversal at cheap prices" — so it tests a normalization choice rather than a distinguishable hypothesis.

critic_notes.target_name: Payout instrument tilted to buybacks when cheap
critic_notes.rationale: Payout *composition* holding total payout roughly fixed is a genuinely distinct construct from the archive's yield and net-issuance designs and the expression matches the hypothesis, though the 0/0 denominator for non-payers will silently cut coverage and the claim of "little HML loading" is overstated given the E/P leg.

critic_notes.target_name: Cheapness with stable financing policy
critic_notes.rationale: The second moment of financing is a legitimately new dimension relative to the archive's level-and-change constructions and the sign logic is coherent, but VOL of net issuance is mechanically dominated by issuance magnitude, so the low-volatility leg risks being a repackaged low-net-issuance sort (a well-documented anomaly) rather than a fragility measure.

critic_notes.target_name: Serial repurchaser at a cash flow discount
critic_notes.rationale: Persistence-versus-intensity is a real and untested distinction here, but the construction is weak — a 0–5 integer count multiplied by a [0,1] rank collapses every non-repurchaser to exactly zero and lets the coarse count dominate the sort, and "consistent repurchaser" outperformance is close to the published repeat-repurchase literature.

critic_notes.target_name: External capital dependence at rich multiples
critic_notes.rationale: Gross equity-plus-debt issuance scaled by assets is essentially the published external financing anomaly (Bradshaw–Richardson–Sloan XFIN, and the composite issuance / overvaluation-issuance literature), and interacting it with a rich price-to-sales multiple is exactly the glamour-issuer cell that literature already documents, so the incremental content is small; gross dltis is also badly contaminated by revolver rollovers.

critic_notes.target_name: Persistent payout mix when cheap
critic_notes.rationale: A clean single-knob horizon extension of the archive's strongest result with a coherent smoothing rationale and a genuine coverage argument; the only caveat is that the three-year denominator still drops permanent non-payers, so the expected coverage gain may be smaller than claimed.

critic_notes.target_name: Sector relative payout mix when cheap
critic_notes.rationale: Economically well-motivated (payout instrument conventions are strongly sector-determined) and internally consistent, but it is a one-operator substitution on the archive's winner and therefore delivers only incremental information relative to Proposal 1.

critic_notes.target_name: Buyback over dividend intensity when cheap
critic_notes.rationale: A legitimate composition-versus-magnitude diagnostic, but since dividends are small relative to repurchases for most firms, (prstkc − dvt)/at collapses to plain repurchase intensity, making this close to the well-known net-repurchase/payout-yield anomaly interacted with earnings yield and near-adjacent to the archive's "Industry neutral cheap repurchaser."

critic_notes.target_name: Equity versus debt retirement when cheap
critic_notes.rationale: A genuinely different decision margin with a bounded, size-neutral construction, but the economic story is weakened by dltr being largely non-discretionary (scheduled maturities, revolver repayments), so the ratio may measure debt-structure mechanics rather than a relative-value choice between claims.

critic_notes.target_name: Pecking order choice at a discount
critic_notes.rationale: Extending instrument choice to the raising side is a sensible, non-duplicative test on a disjoint firm subsample, though dltis is heavily contaminated by revolver draws and rollovers, and the low-earnings-yield leg risks re-expressing the published equity-issuance anomaly through a different scaling.

critic_notes.target_name: Buyback tilted payout among expensive firms
critic_notes.rationale: The stated design ("both legs drawn from the same glamour segment, free of value loading") contradicts what the expression computes — gating produces exact zeros for ~70% of firms, so the short leg is dominated by ungated non-glamour names — and the same INDICATOR-gated glamour cell was already tested in the archive with the opposite expected sign and a mildly positive slope.

critic_notes.target_name: Payout mix with neutral non payers
critic_notes.rationale: The COALESCE-to-zero convention is a defensible neutral placement for non-choosers rather than a pure coverage patch, but the claimed coverage gain is contingent on 0/0 (not NaN inputs) driving the missingness — if prstkc/dvt are absent the fallback is equally undefined — and the resulting large tie block at the midpoint makes this only a modest, partly mechanical variation on the already-tested assets-scaled intensity version.

critic_notes.target_name: Shift toward buybacks when cheap
critic_notes.rationale: The level-versus-change decomposition of the winning mechanism is a legitimate and informative question, though it closely parallels the archive's "Financing policy reversal at cheap prices" (which already differenced a financing flow and produced only t=1.77) and differencing a ratio defined only for payers will further shrink an already 8% coverage sample.

critic_notes.target_name: Payout mix at a composite discount
critic_notes.rationale: Replacing the single E/P leg with a blended earnings-and-book yield is a coherent measurement-error argument and is internally consistent, but it is an incremental swap of one leg of the winning signal rather than a new mechanism, and the stated link to the "generation 1 negative-alpha lesson" is rhetorical rather than substantive.

critic_notes.target_name: Distribute rather than hoard when cheap
critic_notes.rationale: The expression contradicts its hypothesis: with zero payout and a large cash drawdown the ratio hits its maximum of +1, so firms burning cash to fund losses or capex — precisely the distress case the proposal claims to repair — score in the extreme long leg alongside genuine distributors.

critic_notes.target_name: Committed buyback tilt when cheap
critic_notes.rationale: The complementarity test between mix and magnitude is a fair open question, but the added leg is essentially total payout yield — itself a well-known published anomaly and strongly correlated with the E/P leg — so a positive result risks being a repackaged payout-yield/value effect, and multiplying three [0,1] ranks concentrates the long leg in a thin, potentially unstable cell.

critic_notes.target_name: Payout mix against own price history
critic_notes.rationale: Swapping the cross-sectional price benchmark for a within-firm one is the sharpest available test of whether the winning result is managerial timing or amplified HML exposure, and it differs meaningfully from the earlier own-trough signal that paired timing with repurchase intensity rather than instrument choice, though the coarse five-point TS_RANK and the weak alpha of that earlier attempt temper expectations.

critic_notes.target_name: Composite discount with smoothed payout mix
critic_notes.rationale: This is a mechanical stacking of two knobs already tested separately against the same base (composite value leg from gen-4, three-year cumulative mix from gen-3) with no new economic content, so its result will almost certainly interpolate between the two known outcomes and teach little beyond a marginal parameter tune.

critic_notes.target_name: Composite discount with full sample mix
critic_notes.rationale: Also a two-knob combination, but it poses a genuinely decidable question — whether the ~1pt alpha loss from including non-payers came from the extra firms or from noise in the single-multiple E/P leg — which materially affects whether the deployable version is payer-only or universal; note the COALESCE fallback (prstkc−dvt)/at is on a completely different scale than the bounded mix, so non-payers may not in fact land at the intended neutral midpoint after RANK.

critic_notes.target_name: Dilution adjusted payout mix at a discount
critic_notes.rationale: This is a real economic correction rather than a rescaling — distinguishing genuine float reduction from option-offset recycling — the expression matches the hypothesis and preserves the bounded composition form that has driven the alpha, and either outcome is diagnostic about whether the mechanism runs through gross distribution policy or net equity retirement.

critic_notes.target_name: Mix relative to own payout policy at a discount
critic_notes.rationale: The state-versus-deviation question on the financing leg is legitimate and the five-year TS_RANK is the untested middle ground between level and one-year change, but the mix ratio is frequently pinned at exactly +1 or −1 for years at a time, so the within-firm percentile will be heavily tied/degenerate and coverage will fall well below the already-thin 0.079 baseline.

critic_notes.target_name: Three multiple discount with payout mix
critic_notes.rationale: The nested SUMRANK(E/P, SUMRANK(B/M, CF/P)) implicitly weights E/P at one half and each of the other two at one quarter, which contradicts the stated "three multiple" blend, and layering a third correlated value proxy onto an already-strong price leg is a cosmetic extension that will also cut coverage via oancf availability.

critic_notes.target_name: Direction of equity flow at a discount
critic_notes.rationale: Recasting net equity flow as a bounded direction ratio rather than a market-cap-scaled intensity is a substantively different construct that directly tests whether the archive's "composition beats intensity" pattern generalizes beyond the payout margin, and it plausibly relieves the coverage ceiling — though it flirts with the well-documented net share issuance anomaly, so the value interaction must carry the incremental content.

critic_notes.target_name: Firm and equity blended discount with payout mix
critic_notes.rationale: This is a cosmetic stack of two already-tested price legs whose outcome will almost mechanically land between the parents, and the stated motivation (enterprise multiple "unavailable for financial firms") is contradicted by the construction, since nesting the EV ratio inside SUMRANK will if anything shrink rather than extend coverage.

critic_notes.target_name: Net debt enterprise discount with payout mix
critic_notes.rationale: The MIN construction correctly floors net debt at zero so the denominator can never go negative, the change is a single economically motivated correction to the best-performing price leg (cash is both excluded from the operating-business price and the source of buyback funding), and the expression matches the hypothesis exactly — though note it also discards information for net-cash firms, which are precisely the ones the story emphasizes.

critic_notes.target_name: Enterprise discount with full sample mix
critic_notes.rationale: The COALESCE-widened mix has already been crossed with two different price legs in the archive with a consistent result (higher coverage, lower alpha), so a third crossing is a predictable interpolation rather than a new test, and the fallback term is on a completely different scale from the bounded mix so non-payers are placed near the midpoint only by accident of units.

critic_notes.target_name: Cyclically adjusted discount with payout mix
critic_notes.rationale: Smoothing the earnings leg attacks time-series rather than cross-sectional measurement error, which is a genuinely distinct and untested axis and is internally consistent with the expression, but the price leg remains a single conventional multiple so the incremental information over the already-tested E/P and composite versions is likely modest.

critic_notes.target_name: Cheapest claim to retire at a firm level discount
critic_notes.rationale: Re-pairing a weak-but-nonzero decision margin with the strongest price leg is a defensible diagnostic and the expression matches the hypothesis, but the economic premise is shaky because dltr is dominated by scheduled maturities and covenant-driven amortization rather than by any relative-value judgment about which claim is cheaper.

critic_notes.target_name: Payout mix purged of the flexibility motive
critic_notes.rationale: Multiplying by a rank of low earnings volatility does not purge the flexibility motive, it tilts the entire long leg toward low-volatility/quality firms — a separately documented anomaly — so a positive result would be confounded rather than, as the reasoning claims, "evidence about the mechanism"; a within-volatility-bucket interaction or an orthogonalized mix would be the correct test.

critic_notes.target_name: Equity composite discount with wide mix
critic_notes.rationale: This is a near-duplicate of the archive's "Composite discount with full sample mix" (identical price leg, identical wide-mix concept) differing only in the non-payer fallback scaling (SIGN vs. asset-scaled), and given the four surrounding results all cluster at alpha 0.045–0.060 the outcome is almost certainly bounded by its parents rather than the claimed decidable horse race.

critic_notes.target_name: Discretionary payout mix at a firm discount
critic_notes.rationale: Substituting dvc for dvt in the champion changes the signal only for the small minority of firm-years with material preferred dividends, so this is a cosmetic variable swap whose effect will be swamped by noise and cannot deliver the claimed diagnostic about discretion versus capital-structure type.

critic_notes.target_name: Normalized firm level yield with wide mix
critic_notes.rationale: A cyclically adjusted enterprise yield is a genuinely distinct valuation construct rather than a rank blend, and the expression matches the hypothesis, though stacking two already-tested corrections plus the already-tested wide mix makes a large surprise unlikely and the marginal information over the existing enterprise-multiple champion modest.

critic_notes.target_name: Where the incremental payout dollar went
critic_notes.rationale: The marginal-flow composition is a legitimately different construction from the previously tested change-in-ratio and correctly addresses the pinned-at-+1 artifact, but the expression assigns a high score to firms that simply cut dividends (large negative DELTA(dvt)), which is a meaningfully different economic event from redirecting new dollars into buybacks and muddies the stated interpretation.

critic_notes.target_name: Buyback tilt beyond dividend paying tradition
critic_notes.rationale: This is the sharpest remaining robustness question for the champion — whether the mix leg is a disguised never-paid-a-dividend indicator — and the orthogonalization is correctly signed and interpretable either way, with the only caveat that the two legs are nearly deterministically linked for non-dividend payers so the residual may be dominated by rank ties among a narrow subset.

critic_notes.target_name: Payout mix state plus shift at a firm discount
critic_notes.rationale: Averaging the ranks of a level and its own first difference, both already tested against the same price leg, is a standard blend whose result will almost certainly land between the 6% and 2.5% parent alphas, and the claimed complementarity is undercut by the fact that DELTA of a bounded ratio is largely mean-reverting noise for the extreme observations that drive the spread.

critic_notes.target_name: Wide sample discretion residual
critic_notes.rationale: A coherent but largely mechanical union of two already-tested archive elements (the two-term discretion purge and the SIGN-fallback wide mix), justified mainly by coverage rather than by any new economic content, so the informational payoff is modest though the construction is internally consistent.

critic_notes.target_name: Rebalanced discretion residual
critic_notes.rationale: Re-ranking the residual is not a cosmetic monotone relabeling here because the raw residual takes negative values while the price leg is a positive rank — so the sign structure of the interaction genuinely changes — and the diagnosis of thin, unevenly spaced extreme deciles as the source of the low Sharpe is a well-reasoned structural fix rather than a variant.

critic_notes.target_name: Discretion residual purged of scale
critic_notes.rationale: The stated reasoning is backwards — subtracting a market-cap rank inside the purge mechanically raises the score of the smallest firms and therefore pushes microcaps into the long leg, the exact composition instability the proposal claims it prevents — and residualizing on raw size (not industry-relative) confounds the "managerial judgment" interpretation with a size tilt.

critic_notes.target_name: New dollars directed to buybacks
critic_notes.rationale: This is a substantively motivated repair of a diagnosed flaw in the marginal-flow leg (a dividend cut previously masqueraded as a bullish buyback tilt), the positive-part construction matches the hypothesis exactly, and the resulting undefinedness for firms that raised neither payout is an economically correct exclusion rather than a coverage artifact — though the coverage cost should be reported.

critic_notes.target_name: Stale payout mix at a firm discount
critic_notes.rationale: Applying a one-year LAG to an already-tested signal is a trivial variant whose expected outcome (attenuation) teaches little that a decay diagnostic on the existing series could not, and the look-ahead concern it invokes should already be handled by the backtest's fundamental reporting lag.

critic_notes.target_name: Equity priced discretion residual
critic_notes.rationale: A defensible factorial crossing of two previously separated legs with a reasonable argument that the buyback transacts the equity claim, but it is still a price-leg swap on an established design and inherits the unresolved negative-residual-times-positive-rank scaling issue, so its incremental information is limited.

critic_notes.target_name: Wide rebalanced discretion residual
critic_notes.rationale: This is the one defensible next step in a heavily mined family — it combines two independently validated structural fixes (scale-consistent SIGN fallback for non-payers, and re-ranking the residual to remove the sign flip from multiplying a negative residual by a positive price rank) rather than tweaking a knob, and the expression matches the stated hypothesis exactly.

critic_notes.target_name: Wide rebalanced residual with graded commitment
critic_notes.rationale: A clean single-element variation of Proposal 1 with a coherent economic reading (dividend commitment intensity beats an integer payer count, whose ties genuinely degrade rank resolution), but it is a measurement refinement of an already-tested purge rather than new economics, so its value hinges entirely on Proposal 1 being run alongside it.

critic_notes.target_name: Dual priced wide rebalanced residual
critic_notes.rationale: The nested SUMRANK does implement the stated 1/2–1/4–1/4 weighting and blending enterprise with equity multiples has a real rationale (different failure modes for financials and asset-light firms), but choosing the blend weights to match the observed alpha-versus-slope pattern of two prior runs is post-hoc weighting on the same sample and risks manufacturing an average that beats neither leg out of sample.

critic_notes.target_name: Normalized firm yield with rebalanced residual
critic_notes.rationale: Substituting a three-year averaged EBITDA into the price leg is a single, economically motivated knob (management benchmarks against normal earning power) with a sensible complementarity argument against the earnings-volatility purge, but it is close to the boundary of a cosmetic recombination of two already-tested components.

critic_notes.target_name: Standing stance plus fresh allocation
critic_notes.rationale: The complementarity argument is not unreasonable, but this is a five-term kitchen sink that fuses the archive's strongest-slope and strongest-alpha financing legs with no way to attribute the result, and the coverage claim is overstated — the marginal leg still requires a full lagged year of both prstkc and dvt, which the SIGN fallback does not restore, so coverage will fall well short of the 0.110 wide-sample level.

critic_notes.target_name: Short window purge for wider coverage
